headline: アナウンサー is borrowed from English “announcer”.
銅, “copper”, comes from Middle Chinese, and the source compares Min Nan, Wu and Xiang readings.
インタビュー is borrowed from English “interview”.
伸ばす is cognate with 延ばす (nobasu), from the classical verb のぶ (nobu).
スライド is borrowed from English “slide”.
Idea in English, アイデア in Japanese: the source traces it straight to the English word “idea”.
宅, “house, home”, is derived from Middle Chinese 宅 (MC draek).
ブローチ is borrowed from English “brooch”.
銀, “silver”, is from Middle Chinese 銀 (MC ngin), and the source compares Hokkien gîn.
ボート, “rowing boat”, is the English word “boat” in katakana.
でも is で, the て-form of the copula だ/です, plus も (“even; too”).
カロリー is borrowed from French “calorie”.
もしかすると is もしか (“perhaps, if”) plus すると (“doing so”).
カラー is two words in one: the source gives both English “color” and English “collar”.
ファスナー, “fastener, zipper”, is borrowed from English “fastener”.
玉, “ball, sphere, coin”, is recorded simply as from Old Japanese.
カバー is the English word “cover” in katakana.
続々 doubles 続 (zoku), itself from Middle Chinese 續.
スピーチ is borrowed from English “speech”.
売り切れる is 売る (uru, “to sell”) plus 切れる (kireru, “to do completely”).
コート covers two English words: “coat” and “court”.
王, “king”, is from Middle Chinese, and the source gives its sound path as /wau/ to /oː/.
サンダル is borrowed from English “sandal” or French “sandale”; the source does not pick one.
プール, “swimming pool”, is borrowed from English “pool”.
五, “five”, comes from Middle Chinese (MC nguX).
コード traces to three English words: “code”, “cord” and “chord”.
首, “neck”, is from Old Japanese, from Proto-Japonic *kunpi.
スケジュール is borrowed from English “schedule”.
碗, “bowl”, is a Middle Chinese borrowing (MC 'wanX).
トップ is borrowed from English “top”, a doublet of トップス.
膝, “knee, lap”, is from Old Japanese, from Proto-Japonic *pinsa.
